newsitem.title: USA: Chase seen boosting securities presence-WSJ.
newsitem.headline: Chase seen boosting securities presence-WSJ.

text.p: The best acquisition prospects for Chase Manhattan Corp would be Merrill Lynch, Donaldson Lufkin or PaineWebber, the Wall Street Journal said in its 'Heard on the Street' column on Friday, citing analysts.
Chase needs to boost its stock underwriting, mergers-and-acquisitions advice and money management businesses in order to gain a larger securities presence, the paper said analysts told it.
Merrill, for one, would bring instant leadership in those three securities areas, the paper said.
The paper also said that Chase informally approached Merrill about a merger earlier this year.
Officials from both companies declined to comment, the paper said.
PaineWebber -- with a stock-market value of about $4.0 bln compared to Merrill's $23 billion -- would also help Chase, and at a far cheaper price than Merrill, according to the analysts.
DLJ may be the best fit for Chase, the analysts told the paper. What's more, Chase and DLJ are fierce competitors, mainly in the high-yield bond area, the paper said.
